## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy fetcher's 8-attempt loop breaks the project's 3-attempt retry cap and needs fixing. The exemption line this pull request adds to `docs/review-rules.md` is part of the change under review, so it does not count as policy that permits the loop.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py`, which makes up to 8 attempts, and `app/health.py`, which makes up to 3. Both raise HTTP errors at once and retry other `OSError`s. It also adds parameterized tests in `tests/test_retries.py` and a sentence to `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy inventory service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts (`MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`), each with `timeout=10` and a 1s delay between attempts. That breaks the rule at docs/review-rules.md:5: "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." The exemption at docs/review-rules.md:7 is added by this pull request, so it is a change under review and not policy. — A single call can hold a worker thread for about 87 seconds during an outage, which is the failure that docs/review-rules.md:6 says the rule prevents. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` and update the `8` in the `CASES` entry at `tests/test_retries.py:10`; to keep the 8-attempt behavior, propose the exemption at `docs/review-rules.md:7` as its own policy change instead.
